explanations: terra: A staff strikes stone and twelve springs burst from it; striking a hard surface releases concealed matter, an indirect counterpart to hooves striking earth and sparks or soil springing forth.

luna: The section’s ثور dictionary form explains the ox through plowing earth; this cow is explicitly “لَا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ الْأَرْضَ,” not trained to plow it. The negation marks the boundary of the source’s plowing sense. | terra: لَّا ذَلُولٌ تُثِيرُ ٱلْأَرْضَ describes a cow not trained to plow, directly realizing the section's dictionary picture of the ox by which earth is stirred.

terra: After a concealed killing, وَٱللَّهُ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ promises that God will bring out what was hidden; beside the plowing cow of 2:71, it joins soil-working, homicide, and disclosure as the section does.
terra: The slain person is made alive through the cow and كَذَٰلِكَ يُحْىِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمَوْتَى; it completes 2:71-72 by turning a disputed hidden corpse into evidence of resurrection.

luna: The section’s dictionary form describes precious material extracted from stone; this ayah pictures water bursting from split stone. The substance differs, but both make a hidden content emerge from rock.
terra: Rain revives earth after its death while winds and controlled clouds move above it; the ayah brings together stirred atmosphere and hidden terrestrial life emerging from inert ground.

luna: After a ruined town prompts a question about life after death, God restores the traveler’s donkey’s bones and covers them with flesh. This concrete restoration of what has decayed in the earth parallels the section’s dead brought out from graves.

luna: This ayah speaks of good things brought forth from earth and forbids choosing the bad for charity when one would not accept it except reluctantly. It parallels the section’s ore-sifting image through a concrete distinction between valued and inferior produce from earth. | terra: Believers are told to spend from good things and from what God has brought out of the earth, while refusing the bad; the ayah combines terrestrial extraction with discrimination between valuable and inferior material.

terra: Whether people reveal what is within themselves or hide it, God calls them to account for it; disclosure is tied to judgment as in the section's transition from grave contents to chest contents.
terra: Nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God, stating the epistemic boundary that makes both grave contents and breast contents accessible.
terra: Whether people hide مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ or show it, Allah knows it; the ayah gives the concealment/disclosure polarity behind the section's chest-as-deposit image.
terra: Hatred has appeared from hostile mouths while what their breasts conceal is greater, explicitly contrasting a visible sample with a larger inner deposit.
terra: God's purpose is to purify the believers and efface the disbelievers; the purification verb gives a moral counterpart to refining mixed material until its true value is isolated.

terra: لِيَبْتَلِىَ ٱللَّهُ مَا فِى صُدُورِكُمْ وَلِيُمَحِّصَ مَا فِى قُلُوبِكُمْ joins testing breast contents to purification, closely matching the section's image of processing mixed earth to isolate what is truly there.

luna: “يَمِيزَ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ” describes separating bad from good. The section’s dictionary account of “تحصيل” as extracting precious metal from ore supplies a concrete sorting image for this moral distinction. | terra: God does not leave believers in a mixed state حَتَّىٰ يَمِيزَ ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ; this moral separation parallels assaying mixed earth until unlike contents are distinguished.
terra: The condemned wish the earth were levelled over them, yet لَا يَكْتُمُونَ ٱللَّهَ حَدِيثًا; imagined covering by earth cannot prevent disclosure, reversing burial's concealing function.
terra: The brother is killed and the killer becomes a loser; this supplies the corpse whose exposed state creates the first burial problem solved by the crow in 5:31.

luna: The section’s ثور dictionary form describes an ox stirring earth as it searches with its legs; here the raven “يَبْحَثُ فِي الْأَرْضِ” and teaches how to “يُوَارِيَ” the body. Burial opens earth and then covers what it holds, the inverse of the section’s graves opened. | terra: The crow يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ scratches open the soil to teach how to يُوَارِى the brother's body; it supplies both the section's bull-like earth-scratching verb and the concealment branch of the fire-producing root, while burial reverses the grave-opening scene.
terra: A grain in the darknesses of earth is included among what God knows; the tiny hidden terrestrial content joins burial-like concealment to exhaustive divine awareness.
terra: Allah splits seed and date-stone and brings the living from the dead; a closed piece of matter opening to release hidden life parallels the section's soil and grave extraction.

luna: The section explicitly names the concealment sense of its و ر ي root; this ayah uses “وُورِيَ” for what was covered from Adam and his wife. It adds bodily concealment to the section’s burial-and-uncovering image. | terra: The devil seeks لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا, bringing into view what had been concealed; the passive وُۥرِىَ realizes the section's named hiding sense and its reveal/conceal reversal.
luna: After the hidden shame is exposed, this ayah says the pair begin covering themselves with leaves. It completes 7:20’s concealment detail with a specific exposure-then-covering action.
terra: فِيهَا تَمُوتُونَ ... وَمِنْهَا تُخْرَجُونَ locates death in earth and later emergence from it, the same closing and reopening of soil developed in the section.
terra: Rain brings produce out of a dead land and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ, explicitly making emergence from revived soil the model for bringing out the dead.

luna: The section’s ث و ر dictionary entry says locusts take flight; this ayah names locusts among the plagues sent against Pharaoh. The link is limited to the same specific swarm creature: here it is a destructive worldly plague, unlike the resurrection simile in 54:7. | terra: The ayah names ٱلْجَرَادَ among the signs sent against Pharaoh; it securely supplies the same creature as the section's dictionary example, though unlike 54:7 it does not itself say that the locusts rise or spread from graves.
terra: When the stone is struck, twelve springs issue from it, repeating the specific pattern of impact causing a hidden content to break outward.

terra: God separates ٱلْخَبِيثَ مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبِ and piles the bad بَعْضَهُۥ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ; the ayah combines the section's assay-like separation of value with its dictionary picture of mixed goods turned one over another.

luna: The section’s mineral sense names gold and silver recovered from earth; this ayah names people who hoard gold and silver. It turns the extracted treasure into stored wealth whose moral value is exposed by the surrounding judgment warning. | terra: Gold and silver are hoarded rather than spent before being heated in 9:35; this identifies the supposedly precious extracted material whose moral value is reversed by its use.

luna: The next ayah says the hoarded metals are heated in Hellfire and used to brand their owners. It joins the section’s metal and fire images in a reversal where treasure becomes evidence against its possessor. | terra: Hoarded gold and silver are heated in fire and used to brand their owners; the metal treated as precious in the section's mining image becomes an instrument that exposes and punishes misplaced valuation.
terra: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُخْرِجٌ مَّا تَحْذَرُونَ threatens to bring out what hypocrites fear will be exposed from their hearts, an explicit inner analogue to opening graves and extracting ore.
terra: No atom's weight in earth escapes the Lord and nothing smaller or larger lies outside the record, joining concealed matter to exhaustive knowledge.

luna: The people “يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ لِيَسْتَخْفُوا مِنْهُ” fold their breasts to hide, while God knows what they conceal. This gives a bodily concealment image that the section’s chest contents later overturn. | terra: People fold their breasts and cover themselves to hide, yet God knows what they keep secret and disclose; bodily acts of covering fail to keep chest contents inaccessible.
terra: Humanity is produced from earth and settled or enabled to cultivate it, complementing the section's land-working sense of ث و ر and its contrast between worldly development and return to soil.

terra: جَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا turns the town's upper part into its lower; it is the precise spatial converse of the section's dictionary gloss “made its lower part its upper,” giving physical form to total overturning.
terra: The deniers ask whether becoming dust can be followed by a new creation, treating bodily dissolution into earth as the obstacle answered by grave extraction.

luna: The section’s dictionary entry for ح ص ل describes precious metal extracted from ore; this ayah shows metal heated for ornaments or use, with the waste disappearing while what benefits people remains. It gives the extraction and separation image an explicit Qur’anic scene and a criterion of what endures. | terra: Flood foam and smelting dross pass away while useful matter remains; this is the Qur'an's clearest assay image for the section's mining soil being worked until valuable metal is separated from waste.
terra: The deeds of disbelievers are like ash driven violently by wind, a worthless airborne residue contrasting with useful matter that survives the section's separation process.
terra: فَجَعَلْنَا عَٰلِيَهَا سَافِلَهَا repeats the upper-to-lower inversion, the same complete reversal of levels invoked by the section's explanation of بعثر.

luna: This ayah says people extract ornaments from the sea. The section’s dictionary account of metal recovery from mineral soil gives a specific parallel of valuable material drawn from a natural store, with the source here being water rather than earth. | terra: People تَسْتَخْرِجُوا مِنْهُ حِلْيَةً from the sea, a non-mineral parallel in which valuable adornment is extracted from a larger enclosing medium.
terra: Those plotting evil are warned that God may make the earth swallow them, the opposite vertical movement to earth casting out the concealed dead.
terra: The question أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ depicts a girl deliberately hidden in soil; its shameful human act of concealment is morally reversed by the later divine exposure of the buried.
terra: Water sent from heaven gives life to earth after its death, a repeated concrete pattern for apparently inert soil releasing life.
terra: The question whether bones and disintegrated fragments can be raised specifies the altered physical contents that the opened grave must surrender.
terra: The answer to the fragmented-bones objection is that the One who created them first will restore them, preserving personal identity through material dispersal.
terra: People on land are warned that God can cause the ground to swallow them; the secure surface becomes an entrance downward rather than the exit upward pictured by opened graves.

luna: This ayah pictures vegetation from rain drying into chaff that winds scatter. It parallels the section’s named بعثر dictionary sense of dispersing and scattering things, in an earthly scene of what appears and then passes away.

luna: “وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً” depicts the earth laid bare as everyone is gathered, a broader version of the section’s soil turned over and hidden contents exposed. | terra: Mountains are removed, earth is seen exposed, and all people are gathered with none left behind; the stripped surface corresponds to emptied earth revealing every human it had concealed.

luna: After the earth is laid bare and all are gathered, the placed record “لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً” and shows what people did. It parallels the section’s extraction of breast contents by making no small or large item escape the accounting.

terra: A treasure lies beneath the wall until the orphans can يَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنزَهُمَا; a valuable hidden under earth is preserved and later extracted, exactly the buried-treasure model the section gives for grave contents.

luna: “مِنْهَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ ... وَفِيهَا نُعِيدُكُمْ وَمِنْهَا نُخْرِجُكُمْ” gives the earth’s full cycle of origin, return, and renewed emergence that the section’s grave image stages at its end. | terra: Creation from earth, return into it, and a second خروج from it give the complete three-stage movement behind burial and its reversal in the section.

luna: This parallel account says the pair’s nakedness became visible and they began patching leaves over themselves. It repeats the concealment-and-exposure action in a second Qur’anic telling, related to the section’s hidden things brought into view.

terra: On the resurrection day even a mustard seed's weight is brought forth and accounted for; this supplies the exact moral weighing that follows the section's assay-like separation of hidden contents.

luna: This ayah moves from human formation out of dust to dead earth stirred and raised into growth. It joins the section’s earth-turning image to the broader cycle of life emerging from apparently lifeless ground. | terra: Barren earth اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ after rain and brings forth growth; within the argument that leads to raising those in graves, hidden life stirring through soil becomes evidence for human resurrection.

terra: Between the revived-earth demonstration and the promise to raise those in graves, this ayah states that God is truth, gives life to the dead, and is capable of all things; it articulates the inference joining the two scenes.

luna: “يَبْعَثُ مَن فِي الْقُبُورِ” states that God raises those in graves. The section’s note that 100:9 says “what” is in graves rather than “who” makes this person-centered formulation a useful companion to its contents image. | terra: Allah's raising مَن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ states as a resurrection promise what the section renders physically as opening soil and extracting its grave contents.
terra: The people reject the promise that after death and becoming dust and bones they will be brought out, explicitly naming emergence of decomposed grave material.
terra: A repeated objection asks whether people who have become dust and bones will be brought out, closely matching the section's depiction of grave contents extracted from soil.

luna: The section shows graves opened at resurrection; here, after death, “بَرْزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ” sets a barrier until that day. It states the interval that bounds the opening scene. | terra: A barzakh stands behind the dead إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ, defining burial as an interim enclosure with a fixed end rather than a permanent hiding place.
terra: Deeds thought to have value are made into scattered dust; this reverses the section's assay image, in which processing separates lasting value from surrounding earth.
terra: Allah يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ, bringing forth what is hidden in the earth; the act condenses the section's movement from concealment below ground to extraction.
terra: The deniers ask whether they and their ancestors will be brought out after becoming dust, making خروج from earthen dissolution the disputed event.
terra: The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose, restating the section's inner hidden-versus-exposed relation in exact bodily terms.
terra: Nothing absent or hidden in heaven or earth falls outside the clear record, supporting the section's claim that buried contents remain fully recoverable.
terra: The Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they disclose; the repeated formulation supports the section's claim that inner contents cannot remain buried.

luna: Qarun’s treasures have keys heavy enough to burden a group of strong men. This gives a concrete treasure-and-load counterpart to the section’s picture of grave contents as hidden cargo and its extraction of valuable material from earth. | terra: Qarun's treasures have keys heavy for a strong company, making wealth a literal burden before person, house, and riches are swallowed by earth in 28:81; together they invert the section's ejected load and buried treasure.

luna: The earth swallows Qarun and his house. This reverses the section’s direction: there, earth is turned so hidden contents come out; here, a wealthy man and his home disappear into it. | terra: The earth swallows Qarun and his house, moving a person and his wealth downward into concealment; the section's grave and treasure image runs this motion backward by forcing earth to release its load.

luna: After the swallowing in 28:81, people who had wished for Qarun’s position realize that God could have made the earth swallow them too. It completes the wealth-to-earth reversal with the bystanders’ changed judgment of worldly riches.
terra: Among the punished peoples are those whom God caused the earth to swallow, a concise reversal of the section's earth releasing what it contains.
terra: Water revives earth after its death, preserving the section's hidden-to-living movement even though this ayah does not itself state the human resurrection comparison.

luna: The section’s ثور root is explicitly tied to plowing; “وَأَثَارُوا الْأَرْضَ وَعَمَرُوهَا” uses that root for turning and cultivating land. Its worldly building on worked earth sharpens the contrast with earth later opened to expose what it contains. | terra: وَأَثَارُوا ٱلْأَرْضَ uses the same root for earlier peoples' plowing and developing the land; their worldly turning of soil is set inside a warning about their eventual destruction.
terra: God brings living from dead and revives earth after its death, then says وَكَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ; biological extraction, revived soil, and human emergence are made one pattern.
terra: Rain gives life to earth after its death, another occurrence in the same surah that uses changing soil as evidence beside the ث و ر cloud and plowing scenes.

luna: The verse uses the section’s named ث و ر root in “فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا”: winds stir clouds up. It confirms the root’s stirring or raising action in a different medium, extending the image from hooves and soil to wind and cloud. | terra: Winds فَتُثِيرُ سَحَابًا use the section's ث و ر root for setting a previously still mass in motion, the same core movement behind hooves raising soil.

luna: This ayah says God revives the earth after its death and explicitly likens that to raising the dead. It supplies a direct life-from-earth parallel to the section’s graves opened and hidden contents raised. | terra: The command to look at how God revives earth after its death concludes that He revives the dead, turning the worked soil image into resurrection evidence.

terra: Even a mustard seed hidden in a rock, the heavens, or the earth يَأْتِ بِهَا ٱللَّهُ; the minute concealed content is recovered, and the ending ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ echoes the section's final divine awareness.

terra: People return to God, are told what they did, and He is عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ; return, disclosure of deeds, and knowledge of breasts form the same eschatological sequence as opened graves and processed hearts.
terra: The deniers ask whether, after becoming lost within the earth, they can enter a new creation; this identifies the resurrection problem as bodily matter dispersed into its earthen container.
terra: Water is driven to barren land and crops are brought out for people and livestock, a direct agricultural instance of useful content extracted from earth.
terra: God knows what enters the earth and what emerges from it, directly matching the movement from a body placed below ground to grave contents brought out.
terra: In an oath about the coming Hour, not even an atom's weight in earth escapes the Lord and all is recorded; hidden terrestrial minuteness cannot evade later accounting.
terra: Deniers are warned that God could make the earth swallow them, setting downward concealment against the resurrection scene of bodies forced back out.

luna: The verse says God revives earth after its death and then “كَذَٰلِكَ النُّشُورُ.” This is a nonlexical parallel to the section’s hidden thing erupting from earth and the dead being brought out. | terra: Winds تُثِيرُ سَحَابًا, then the cloud revives dead land, and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلنُّشُورُ; it joins the named root's stirring sense to resurrection from earth.

luna: The ayah contrasts fresh and salt waters, then says people extract wearable ornaments from them. It repeats the extraction image with a distinct focus on the two sources and the valuables each yields. | terra: From the two seas people تَسْتَخْرِجُونَ حِلْيَةً; the repeated extraction of valuable adornment clarifies the section's concrete mining sense of separating treasure from surrounding matter.
terra: Those فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ cannot presently be made to hear; this closed, silent grave state is the temporal boundary reversed when graves are opened and their occupants emerge.
terra: God revives dead earth and أَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهَا حَبًّا, bringing grain out of it; the soil releases a useful hidden content just as graves and mineral earth yield what they hold.

luna: At the trumpet, people stream “مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ”; this directly stages the emergence from graves that 100:9 describes as grave contents overturned. | terra: At the trumpet blast people rush مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ to their Lord, a direct staging of occupants extracted from their burial places.

luna: The awakened speakers ask “مَن بَعَثَنَا مِن مَرْقَدِنَا” (“who raised us from our resting place?”). That word for resting place echoes the section’s qabr dictionary sense, while their question voices the shock of the graves opening. | terra: Those emerging in 36:51 ask who raised them from their resting place and are told this is the Merciful's promise, interpreting the opened burial place as promised resurrection rather than mere disturbance.
terra: The objector displays a decayed bone and asks who can revive it, turning the physical remainder associated with a grave into the test case for resurrection.
terra: The answer says the One who originated the bones will revive them and knows every creation, joining restoration of buried remains to the knowledge motif of the section.

terra: God makes fire for people from a green tree, so an apparently contrary material releases latent flame; this nonlexically develops the section's sense of fire as something struck or brought forth from concealment.
terra: The resurrection objection names death, dust, and bones before asking whether people will be raised, specifying what lies behind the section's content-like grave grammar.
terra: حَتَّىٰ تَوَارَتْ بِٱلْحِجَابِ uses the section's named تَوَارَى form for disappearing behind a veil, showing the hiding branch of و ر ي in a setting distinct from covering a corpse with soil.
terra: On the resurrection day people are fully exposed and nothing concerning them is hidden from God, the human result of the section's physical and inward uncovering.

luna: “وَمَا تُخْفِي الصُّدُورُ” names what breasts conceal, matching the section’s image of extracting “what is in the breasts” and its discussion of the source section’s concealment sense under و ر ي. | terra: God knows مَا تُخْفِى ٱلصُّدُورُ, naming breasts specifically as containers of concealed material that remains accessible to divine knowledge.
luna: When people ask their skins why they testified, the skins answer that God made them speak. The body’s own hidden witness is exposed, complementing the section’s extraction of what lies within.

luna: “وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَسْتَتِرُونَ” recalls their attempt to hide from the testimony of hearing, sight, and skin, then says they wrongly thought God did not know much of their deeds. It reverses the section’s concealment root into failed concealment at disclosure.
terra: Humbled earth اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ when watered, and its reviver is said to revive the dead; the formerly sunken surface moving and swelling answers the section's hidden-then-rising motion.
terra: Measured water revives a dead land and كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ explicitly maps that emergence onto human resurrection.
terra: Provision sent from heaven revives earth after its death, making lifeless ground a receptacle whose latent outcome is brought forth.
terra: Those with diseased hearts suppose that God will not يُخْرِجَ ٱللَّهُ أَضْغَٰنَهُمْ; the verb turns concealed rancor into something extracted from an inner container.

luna: “مَا تَنقُصُ الْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ” says God knows what earth consumes from the dead and keeps it in a preserving record. The burial that hides or diminishes the body cannot erase the contents later brought out. | terra: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ answers the problem of bodies consumed in soil with divine knowledge, directly complementing the question about knowing when grave contents are brought out.
terra: Rain revives بَلْدَةً مَّيْتًا and the ayah concludes كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلْخُرُوجُ, naming renewed earth as the likeness of the خروج from burial developed in the section.

luna: “تَشَقَّقُ الْأَرْضُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا” depicts the earth splitting away from people as they hurry out, a direct scene of buried people emerging from the ground. | terra: The earth تَشَقَّقُ عَنْهُمْ سِرَاعًا, splitting away from people as they emerge rapidly; this is the grave soil physically opening and surrendering what it held.

luna: The section’s ثور dictionary entry names locusts taking flight as an eruption; here people stream from graves “كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ,” making that secondary sense an explicit resurrection image. | terra: People come out of the graves كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ; the ayah fuses the section's grave extraction with its named secondary image of locusts springing into motion.
terra: Pearls and coral emerge from the two waters, another Qur'anic scene in which valuable material comes forth from an encompassing medium.
terra: إِذَا رُجَّتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ رَجًّا makes earth itself violently convulse on the last day, enlarging the hoof-broken surface into an eschatological ground upheaval.
terra: Mountains are pulverized immediately after earth convulses, supplying the solid material that becomes airborne dust in the next ayah.
terra: فَكَانَتْ هَبَآءً مُّنۢبَثًّا turns pulverized ground into scattered dust in the air, a large-scale counterpart to hooves breaking the surface and raising its particles.
terra: The question whether death, dust, and bones can be followed by resurrection again identifies the grave's transformed physical contents.
terra: The first and later generations are to be gathered at an appointed time, answering 56:47 by ensuring that no layer of the earth's accumulated dead remains uncollected.
terra: أَفَرَءَيْتُمُ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى تُورُونَ uses the same و ر ي root in its fire-kindling branch, which the section deliberately sets beside that root's concealment branch.
terra: God knows what enters the earth and what comes out of it; this gives the section's burial-and-extraction movement as a single polarity under divine knowledge.
terra: God's reviving of earth after its death is offered as a sign to understand, supporting the section's passage from disturbed soil to the recovery of the dead.

terra: The ayah compares despair of the hereafter with despair concerning the occupants of graves; it presents the closed grave as an apparent boundary of hope that the section's opening of graves overturns.

luna: “مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ” and “بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ” join concealed and declared things to what is in breasts, the same hidden-to-exposed interior that the section develops. | terra: God knows what people conceal and reveal and is عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ, explicitly locating the hidden deposit in breasts.
terra: Concealed or open speech is equally known because إِنَّهُۥ عَلِيمٌۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ, directly pairing secrecy with knowledge of the inner deposit that the section pictures as extracted.

terra: أَلَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ خَلَقَ answers 67:13's concealed-speech scene by grounding knowledge in creation and ending ٱللَّطِيفُ ٱلْخَبِيرُ, close to the section's final insistence on the Lord's awareness.
terra: The threat that earth may swallow people while it heaves joins ingestion and violent ground movement, reversing the section's heaving earth that surrenders its contents.

luna: Here earth and mountains are carried and crushed in one crushing blow, in the same judgment passage that later presents people with nothing hidden. The terrain’s violent overturning intensifies the section’s image of earth opened at the end. | terra: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one crushing, presenting final ground upheaval as a total mechanical overturning of solid terrain.

luna: “لَا تَخْفَىٰ مِنكُمْ خَافِيَةٌ” says nothing about people remains hidden when they are presented, clarifying the section’s movement from concealed grave and breast contents to disclosure. | terra: On the day people are presented, no hidden thing belonging to them remains hidden; it states the complete exposure toward which the opened graves and processed breasts move.

luna: This ayah says people come swiftly out of graves on the Day, directly staging the grave opening described in the section and adding their hurried movement toward the gathering. | terra: They emerge مِنَ ٱلْأَجْدَاثِ سِرَاعًا, making the section's overturned grave contents a rapidly moving human multitude.

luna: Immediately after the grave emergence in 70:43, this ayah says their eyes are humbled and disgrace covers them. It adds the exposed people’s condition, a reversal of earthly confidence before the final disclosure.

luna: “أَنبَتَكُم مِّنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا” pictures human life emerging from earth like growth. This parallels the section’s named ثور dictionary sense, “eruption of something,” and its movement from buried matter to emergence. | terra: Allah caused humanity to grow from the earth like vegetation; paired with return and extraction in 71:18, it makes soil both origin and temporary repository.

luna: “يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا” completes the plant-from-earth image with return and extraction, a close account of the burial and re-emergence sequence. | terra: Allah returns humans into the earth and then يُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا, stating burial and forceful extraction in the same ayah.
terra: Earth and mountains quake and the mountains become a loose mound of sand, a judgment-day counterpart to solid ground broken into mobile particles.
terra: The human supposes that God will not gather his bones; the ayah identifies disassembled bodily remains as recoverable grave content rather than irretrievable debris.
terra: God is able even to proportion the fingertips, completing 75:3's answer by showing that extraction and gathering do not blur the identity of what earth held.

luna: The section calls a grave the dead person’s resting place and hidden hollow; “أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا” extends that containing image from grave to earth. | terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ ٱلْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا presents earth as a containing receptacle, matching the section's focus on graves as lowered, concealed storage.

luna: This next ayah identifies the earth’s gathered contents as “أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا.” It completes 77:25’s receptacle image and clarifies how earth holds the dead whose contents the section sees turned out. | terra: أَحْيَآءً وَأَمْوَٰتًا identifies the living and the dead as what earth gathers into the receptacle named in 77:25, restoring persons behind the section's content-like مَا.
terra: The objection أَءِذَا كُنَّا عِظَٰمًا نَّخِرَةً identifies decayed bones as the material awaiting the sudden return to the surface in 79:14, specifying what the grave contains.
terra: The single زَجْرَةٌ triggers the sudden appearance on the surface in 79:14, supplying the release event for the section's hidden-to-exposed movement.
terra: After a single blast, فَإِذَا هُم بِٱلسَّاهِرَةِ places the dead suddenly upon the open surface, the endpoint of the section's movement from concealed depth to exposed ground.

luna: “فَأَقْبَرَهُ” says God places the person in a grave, matching the section’s dictionary sense of qabr as the dead person’s resting place and the covered state that the later turning reverses. | terra: ثُمَّ أَمَاتَهُۥ فَأَقْبَرَهُ makes burial itself an act in the divinely ordered human sequence and supplies the section's ق ب ر root in its literal resting-place sense.

luna: “إِذَا شَاءَ أَنشَرَهُ” completes the preceding burial with God’s later raising of the person, the opening movement developed in the section’s “بعثر” image. | terra: After God causes the person to be buried in 80:21, ثُمَّ إِذَا شَآءَ أَنشَرَهُ reverses that placement by raising him whenever He wills.

luna: In the food-and-crops passage, this ayah says God splits the earth open; the following verses show grain and other growth emerging. It gives a literal soil-opening scene parallel to the section’s turned ground, though for cultivation rather than graves. | terra: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا ٱلْأَرْضَ شَقًّا pictures earth deliberately split so that what follows can emerge, an agricultural counterpart to broken grave soil.
terra: After the earth is split in 80:26, grain is made to grow in it; this ayah identifies the useful content released by the opened agricultural soil.
terra: وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ brings a buried girl forward as a questioned moral subject; it restores personhood where burial had reduced a human being to concealed earth-content.
terra: بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ gives the buried girl a charge to answer through no fault of her own, completing 81:8's reversal from concealed object to vindicated person.
terra: The scrolls are spread open in the same judgment sequence as the buried girl is questioned, giving documentary form to hidden contents being unfolded for inspection.
terra: The sky splitting begins the sequence that reaches grave overturning in 82:4; one enclosing boundary after another gives way before hidden grave contents do.
terra: Stars scatter immediately before seas burst and graves are overturned; their dispersal parallels the section's dictionary sense of a load broken up and strewn about.
terra: The seas are made to burst forth just before the graves are overturned, extending the scene of breached containers releasing what had been held within.

luna: This repeats the section’s named بعثر root in “بُعْثِرَتْ” for graves overturned. It gives the same hidden grave contents a second, explicit Qur’anic staging. | terra: وَإِذَا ٱلْقُبُورُ بُعْثِرَتْ repeats the section's exact grave-overturning verb and scene outside surah 100.

luna: Immediately after 82:4 overturns the graves, this ayah says each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind. It supplies the moral contents made visible by the upheaval, parallel to 100:10’s opened breasts. | terra: Immediately after the graves are overturned in 82:4, each soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind; this makes explicit the same passage from opened graves to disclosed knowledge that 100:9 frames with “does he not know?”

luna: “وَإِذَا الْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ” describes earth spread out immediately before 84:4 says it casts out what is within and empties. This ayah supplies the opened, flattened ground that frames the section’s contents emerging. | terra: وَإِذَا ٱلْأَرْضُ مُدَّتْ stretches the earth immediately before it casts out its contents, establishing the transformed ground on which the section's “what is in it” scene occurs.

luna: “أَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ” describes earth throwing out what is in it and emptying; this closely matches the section’s focus on the contents concealed in graves. | terra: وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا وَتَخَلَّتْ makes the stretched earth cast out “what is in it” and empty itself, an exact parallel to the section's attention to مَا فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ as contained matter.
terra: وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُوعُونَ treats what deniers harbor as something stored up in a container, a close conceptual match for inner contents accumulated and then exposed.

luna: “يَوْمَ تُبْلَى السَّرَائِرُ” names the testing and exposure of hidden secrets, closely matching the section’s account of what is in the breasts being extracted. | terra: يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ makes the resurrection day a testing and exposure of secrets, directly corresponding to the section's ore-like extraction of what chests conceal.
terra: وَٱلْأَرْضِ ذَاتِ ٱلصَّدْعِ presents earth by its capacity to fissure, the same opening of a formerly continuous surface required by the section's plowing and unburial images.
luna: “وَتُحِبُّونَ الْمَالَ حُبًّا جَمًّا” gives an explicit parallel to Surah 100’s intense love of wealth, which immediately precedes the image of graves and inner contents exposed.

luna: “دُكَّتِ الْأَرْضُ دَكًّا دَكًّا” follows the statement of intense love of wealth in 89:20. Its pounded earth pairs worldly wealth with the section’s upheaved ground and the judgment that uncovers what it held. | terra: On judgment day the earth is pounded repeatedly, a forceful breaking and reworking of the ground that enlarges the section's hoof-struck surface into an eschatological event.

luna: The earth’s “زِلْزَالَهَا” is the convulsion that precedes the burdens’ emergence in 99:2, completing the ground upheaval named by that neighboring ayah. | terra: The earth's own violent earthquake initiates the sequence whose next act is ejecting its burdens, so it supplies the ground-upheaval immediately preceding the section's extraction image.

luna: “وَأَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا” makes earth itself eject its burdens, a direct parallel to the section’s turned soil and “what is in the graves” brought out. | terra: وَأَخْرَجَتِ ٱلْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا pictures the earth ejecting its burdens, matching the section's treatment of those in graves as contents or a load brought out of soil.

luna: After earth ejects its burdens in 99:2, people ask what has happened to it. That bewildered response complements the section’s “does he not know?” question about grave contents being brought out.

luna: After earth ejects its burdens in 99:2, “تُحَدِّثُ أَخْبَارَهَا” gives the earth a further act of disclosure: it reports its news. This extends the section’s image of the ground no longer keeping its contents hidden. | terra: After earth ejects its burdens, it recounts its news; the opened ground becomes a witness rather than a silent cover, extending the section's move from concealment to knowledge.

luna: After 99:4 says earth reports its news, this ayah attributes that disclosure to the Lord’s inspiration. It adds the divine source behind the earth’s testimony, alongside the section’s final notice that the Lord is fully informed.

luna: This ayah says people come forth in separate groups to be shown their deeds. It carries 99:1–4’s earth upheaval into the exposure of human actions, parallel to the section’s sequence from opened graves to extracted breast contents. | terra: People issue forth in separate groups to be shown their deeds after earth has expelled its loads, identifying the ejected contents with accountable persons and their inner record.

luna: After the earth’s upheaval and report, this ayah says the one who did an atom’s weight of good “يَرَهُ.” It makes the disclosure fine-grained, like the section’s account of extracting and separating what was hidden. | terra: The smallest weight of good is made visible after the earth's upheaval, giving a moral assay to the section's image of separating value from worked material.

luna: This parallel continuation says the one who did an atom’s weight of evil “يَرَهُ.” The matching good-and-evil pair specifies what the exposure in 99:7 reveals. | terra: The smallest weight of evil is likewise made visible, completing the assay-like disclosure rather than allowing any hidden residue to remain mixed in.

luna: This pictures people like “الْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ,” scattered moths, while the section’s ثور dictionary sense names locusts and 54:7 uses them for people streaming from graves. The insects differ, but both are specific swarm images for the final human gathering. | terra: On the resurrection day people are كَٱلْفَرَاشِ ٱلْمَبْثُوثِ, a dispersed insect multitude that nonlexically parallels the section's locusts springing up and 54:7's grave-emergence swarm.

luna: “أَلْهَاكُمُ التَّكَاثُرُ” opens a sequence in which rivalry for more leads, in the next ayah, to visiting graves. This joins worldly accumulation to the section’s turn from intense love of wealth to grave contents brought out.

luna: “زُرْتُمُ الْمَقَابِرَ” makes grave-visiting the endpoint of rivalry in accumulation. The visit by the living contrasts with the section’s graves opened and contents extracted, while the sequence links both to wealth. | terra: حَتَّىٰ زُرْتُمُ ٱلْمَقَابِرَ calls entry into graves a “visit”; this makes the grave a temporary stopping place, consistent with the section's lexical description of it as a station that will be opened again.
luna: The person “جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ” accumulates and counts wealth, echoing Surah 100’s intense love of wealth before graves are opened and breast contents extracted.

luna: The wealth collector “يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ” thinks his property will make him last forever. This is a sharp boundary against the section’s graves opened and inner contents exposed after the wealth-centered life.
